title: Measurement incompatibility in Bayesian quantum estimation beyond quadratic loss
authors: Francesco Albarelli, Stefano Chessa, Jesús Rubio
abstract: In single-shot Bayesian multiparameter quantum estimation, measurement incompatibility can increase the minimum joint quadratic loss by at most a factor of two relative to the bound obtained by optimising each parameter separately. Using the generalised Barnum--Knill inequality, we establish the same bound for a wider class of additive losses generated by positive score functions, showing that this limitation extends beyond the standard quadratic setting. To illustrate this result, we consider a broad family of periodic losses, including the sine loss sometimes employed in interferometry, and derive the corresponding incompatibility bound for Bayesian multiphase estimation with arbitrary prior knowledge. We further extend the framework to unbounded losses, such as absolute losses; this also recovers the case of quadratic losses.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates measurement incompatibility in quantum parameter estimation, extending established bounds beyond the standard quadratic loss. Using the generalized Barnum-Knill inequality, the authors prove that the factor-of-two limitation on the achievable precision holds for a wide class of additive losses, including periodic and absolute losses. This result significantly broadens the applicability of quantum metrology bounds to more realistic sensing scenarios.
main_problem: The paper quantifies the limitation imposed by measurement incompatibility in Bayesian multiparameter quantum estimation theory (QET). It seeks to extend the known bounds beyond the standard quadratic loss setting.
main_result: The factor-of-two limitation on measurement incompatibility, previously established for quadratic loss, extends to any additive loss whose individual contributions are generated by positive score functions. This is formalized by the bound $\mathcal{L}_{	ext{IF}} \le \mathcal{L}_{	ext{opt}} \le \mathcal{L}(M_{	ext{PGM}}) \le 2 \mathcal{L}_{	ext{IF}}$.
method: The analysis utilizes the generalized Barnum–Knill (BK) inequality and extends the framework from quadratic losses to general additive losses defined by positive score functions. The method involves Fourier analysis for periodic losses and taking limits for unbounded losses.
model_or_system: The study is set in the general quantum state $ho( oldsymbol{	heta})$ parameterized by $ oldsymbol{	heta} \in \Omega$, analyzed using Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs) $\{M(	ilde{ oldsymbol{	heta}})\}$. The estimation involves an additive loss function $\ell(	ilde{ oldsymbol{	heta}},  oldsymbol{	heta}) = \sum w_j \ell_j(	ilde{	heta}_j, 	heta_j)$.
key_observables: Minimum joint loss ($\mathcal{L}_{	ext{opt}}$), Incompatibility-free benchmark loss ($\mathcal{L}_{	ext{IF}}$), and the incompatibility quantifier ($\xi$).
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the parameter space ($d$), the weights $w_j$, and the specific form of the loss function (e.g., periodic or absolute losses).
main_assumptions: The loss function must be additive, and the individual loss components must be derived from positive score functions $\sigma_j$ for the main theorem to hold.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general bound using positive scores, extending the factor-of-two limit from quadratic loss. It then applies this to specific families of losses, including periodic (sine loss) and unbounded (absolute loss) cases, confirming the robustness of the bound.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous generalization of fundamental quantum metrology bounds, showing that the limitations imposed by measurement incompatibility are not restricted to simple quadratic metrics, which is crucial for analyzing complex quantum sensing protocols.
